pillars: Hairline protection, Scalp hygiene, Targeted serum cadence, Friction reduction
objective: Create a consistent hairline-care protocol that reduces traction and friction, supports scalp hygiene, conditions fragile hair around the edges, and documents changes over time.
starting_assessment_fields: Hairline condition (fullness, short hairs, sparse areas); Temples (left & right separately); Breakage (short broken vs. shed hairs); Scalp (flaking, itching, redness, tenderness); Styling history (braids, wigs, ponytails, slick styles); Friction sources (bonnets, scarves, headbands, pillowcases); Current products; Baseline photos (front, left temple, right temple).
core_cadence_summary: Scalp cleansing: Once weekly; Targeted scalp serum: Daily or product-directed; Hairline conditioning: Every wash; Low-tension styling: Daily; Friction protection: Every night; Progress monitoring: Every 2 weeks (photos at baseline, Week 4, Week 8).
success_measurements: Reduced exposure to tight hairstyles; Consistent serum use; Less hairline tenderness/irritation; Reduced avoidable breakage; Improved hairline manageability; Comparable photographic documentation.
editorial_promise_and_guardrails: Promise: A more consistent, protective hairline-care routine and a better record of changes. Medical guardrail: Seek a dermatologist if there are smooth/shiny bald areas, progressive recession, loss of follicular openings, pain, inflammation, or patchy shedding.

pillars: Growth support (scalp cleansing, targeted serum, scalp inspection) + Length retention (hydration, conditioning, lipids/ceramides, protein, bond care, low-manipulation)
objective: Support consistent scalp care while improving the condition and protection of the hair fiber so that more of the hair's naturally produced length can be retained.
starting_assessment_fields: Current length (front, sides, crown, back); Hair density (low, medium, high); Strand characteristics (fine, medium, coarse); Scalp condition (oiliness, flakes, buildup, irritation); Breakage areas; Ends condition (tangling, splitting, thin ends); Moisture & manageability; Styling history; Current regimen; Standardized baseline photos & length measurement.
core_cadence_summary: Scalp cleansing: Weekly; Targeted scalp serum: Daily or product-directed; Moisturizing conditioner & leave-in: Every wash; Deep conditioner & ceramide/lipid support: Weekly; Bond-supporting treatment: Weeks 3 & 6 (or Weeks 2 & 6 per label); Protein checkpoint: Week 4 (if hair profile supports it); Overnight protection: Nightly; Growth tracking & photos: Baseline, Week 4, Week 8.
success_measurements: Comparable length photographs (Weeks 1, 4, 8); Scalp condition; Breakage observations; End condition; Manageability; Routine adherence; Product tolerance.
editorial_promise_and_guardrails: Promise: A structured approach to scalp care and length retention, not a guaranteed growth rate (scalp hair averages ~0.5 in/month). Cosmetic serum is not a substitute for clinically established medical hair-loss treatment.

pillars: Moisture & hydration, Cuticle conditioning, Biweekly lipid/ceramide support, Scheduled protein checkpoints, Damage-focused bond care
objective: Establish a deliberate conditioning strategy that improves softness, manageability, hydration, and hair-fiber resilience while incorporating appropriate protein and lipid treatments.
starting_assessment_fields: Dryness timing (when hair begins feeling dry); Tangling hotspots; Breakage zones; Elasticity response to stretching (non-diagnostic); Strand characteristics (fine, medium, coarse); Porosity (self-assessed, noting limitations); Chemical/heat history (coloring, relaxing, bleaching, heat); Current products.
core_cadence_summary: Gentle cleansing: Weekly; Rinse-out conditioner & leave-in: Every wash; Deep conditioning: Weekly; Lipid/ceramide support: Every 2 weeks (Weeks 2 & 6); Protein treatment checkpoints: Weeks 3 & 7; Bond-supporting treatment: Week 5 (more frequent if severely damaged); Progress assessment: Every 2 weeks (photos at baseline, Week 4, Week 8).
success_measurements: Dryness score (1–5); Tangling score (1–5); Breakage observations; Manageability score (1–5); Product tolerance; Deep-conditioning consistency; Protein-treatment response; Photographic comparison.
editorial_promise_and_guardrails: Promise: A more deliberate and consistent conditioning regimen, with better insight into how hair responds to different treatments. Guardrail: Do not diagnose protein deficiency from feel alone; use practical observations (stiff vs. limp vs. coated) to adjust cosmetic care.
